title: What are Conditional Statements?
overview: Conditional statements allow JavaScript programs to make decisions based on different conditions. They execute specific code when a condition is true or false.

title: if Statement
overview: The if statement executes a block of code only when the given condition evaluates to true.

example.title: if Example

title: if...else Statement
overview: The if...else statement is used when we want to execute one block of code when a condition is true and another block when the condition is false.

example.title: if...else Example

title: else if Statement
overview: The else if statement is used when multiple conditions need to be checked. JavaScript evaluates conditions from top to bottom.

example.title: else if Example

title: Switch Statement
overview: The switch statement is used to execute different code blocks based on different possible values. It is useful when checking multiple fixed conditions.

example.title: Switch Example

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how conditional statements help JavaScript make decisions using if, if...else, else if, and switch statements.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Conditions control program flow.
✔ if runs code when condition is true.
✔ else handles false conditions.
✔ else if checks multiple conditions.
✔ switch handles multiple fixed cases.
